route.text: Apply through Common App. Normally, prior matriculation after school requires a transfer application. Dartmouth expressly permits international students enrolled at a university in their home country to choose first-year entry: include that transcript and reasons; previous university credit will not transfer. A prior bachelor's degree makes an applicant ineligible.

fee.waiver: Request a hardship waiver in Common App. International applicants qualify under the stated economic-need criteria; follow the counselor confirmation instructions. Contact Admissions if you cannot use the listed criteria.

testing.text: Testing is required. U.S. high-school students submit SAT or ACT. Students schooled outside the U.S. may instead submit three AP exams, predicted/final IB Diploma or A-level results, or final qualifying national-exam results. School officials must send predictions; national predictions do not qualify. SAT/ACT are superscored and may be self-reported, with official verification before enrollment.

scores.population: Enrolled first-year students who submitted the relevant test.
scores.note: Historical ranges describe a cohort, not an admission threshold.

english.text: Required when English is not your first language and you have fewer than two years of English-medium curriculum. No required minimum. Successful applicants typically exceed IELTS 7, DET 135, Cambridge 185, or old-scale TOEFL 100; new-scale TOEFL 5 or higher. TOEFL MyBest and Essentials are not accepted.

tests.name: IELTS
tests.condition: Most successful applicants score above 7; not a minimum.

tests.name: TOEFL iBT
tests.condition: 5 or higher for tests from January 21, 2026.

waiver.rule: The requirement applies only if English is not the first language AND the curriculum has not been in English for at least two years.

selection.text: Dartmouth reads academic preparation and personal context together. Testing supports the school record and recommendations but is not the primary factor. The whole application, including contribution and experiences, matters.

funding.text: Need-blind first-year admission includes international students. Dartmouth meets calculated need with scholarships and employment, without required student loans. No award amount follows automatically from your own budget.
funding.forms: CSS Profile code 3351, or ISFAA for serious fee hardship. Submit signed 2025 parent tax/income statements in the original currency with English translations; applicants may translate aid documents themselves. Parents living in the US use the applicable IDOC path. Non-filer and noncustodial-parent waiver forms apply only where relevant.
funding.renewal: Reapply using the Dartmouth Renewal Application in DartHub and parent tax/income records selected by parents’ residence. General renewal deadline: April 1; the Scholarship Matching Survey follows in summer. Need is reassessed annually and term enrollment changes the budget.
funding.exceptions: FAFSA is for eligible US citizens/permanent residents. Non-Canadian internationals have no first-year summer earnings expectation, but later years carry a work contribution; employment is not a grant. Major-specific merit awards are not established by this need-based policy.

costs.exclusions: Three-term published baseline. Extra first-year charges: $269 records/class dues and $250 orientation meals. Insurance $5,216 unless waived; basic computer $1,700 if needed. Travel depends on home address. The page says a $250 minimum travel allowance is included, although the listed categories already sum to $98,427; confirm the individualized budget.

testing.text: SAT and ACT are optional. Choose separately whether each test is considered, and change that choice by the application deadline. Self-reports are accepted and verified for enrolling students. SAT and ACT are superscored; the current ACT composite uses English, Reading and Math, with Science optional. Official reports may come from a counselor or testing agency. Codes: SAT 3089; ACT 1636.

scores.population: Enrolled first-year students who submitted the relevant test.
scores.note: CDS 2025–26 C9. Test-optional score submitters are not the entire entering class; this range is not a cutoff.

english.text: English test scores are optional, with no qualifying minimum. TOEFL, IELTS, DET and Cambridge results may be self-reported. Submitted English scores cannot be removed. All entering students still need college-level English; Bowdoin has no ESL courses.

selection.text: The academic record carries the greatest emphasis in Bowdoin’s current description. Readers consider intellectual curiosity, engagement and how applicants use available opportunities, alongside writing, recommendations and respect for differing perspectives.

funding.text: Bowdoin meets admitted international students' demonstrated need through scholarship and a small campus-work expectation.
funding.forms: For non-Canadian Class of 2031 applicants, submit aid materials only after admission using the individualized instructions. Canadian applicants submit the 2027–28 CSS Profile (3089), 2025 parent tax/income records, T1 and T4 via IDOC.
funding.renewal: Returning students follow a separate annual process. Current international students use CSS, or ISFAA if access or cost prevents CSS submission.
funding.exceptions: The returning-student CSS/ISFAA instruction is not the initial application checklist for non-Canadian Class of 2031 applicants. FAFSA is not required of ineligible international students.

costs.exclusions: The $97,900 baseline includes $95,400 billed comprehensive fees and $2,500 books/personal costs. Transportation is excluded; personal spending varies. Insurance premium and waiver details require confirmation.

english.text: English testing is highly recommended for international applicants without English as a first/home language or the primary language throughout secondary school. The listed expected minima apply in most cases within that recommendation, not as a universal testing mandate. Official verification of self-reports is required by May 2027 for Fall 2027 entrants; send reports before expiration.

waiver.rule: Testing is highly recommended when English is neither a first/home language nor the primary language throughout secondary school. No universal numeric schooling-duration exemption is stated.

selection.text: Brown evaluates achievement in the context of the applicant’s schooling and opportunities, without favoring one national system. Academic preparation, intellectual curiosity, initiative, writing and the potential to contribute inform the review. Historical CDS C7 column categories could not be verified from the interactive dashboard.

funding.text: First-year international applicants are need-blind from the Fall 2025 admission cohort. Aid eligibility for earlier cohorts follows their original policy. Brown meets demonstrated need through need-based aid, with no institutional merit awards. Work expectations and loans are distinct from scholarship.
funding.forms: Electronic CSS Profile (3189); separate parent forms after divorce/separation. IDOC income documents only if requested. 2025 tax/non-filer and employer earnings records may be requested.
funding.renewal: Returning international students, including Canadians, use the personalized requirements in Banner Self-Service. Contact Financial Aid after a leave or when applying for aid for the first time. The original admission cohort determines whether the older need-aware restrictions apply; do not copy the domestic FAFSA renewal checklist.
funding.exceptions: Brown offers no CSS fee waivers and does not accept ISFAA or paper CSS instead. Applicants in Iran or North Korea must contact financial aid for an alternative. No FAFSA for ineligible international applicants.

costs.exclusions: The $99,994 total excludes books for BCMS participants, personalized travel and health insurance. Nonparticipants budget an additional $1,300 for books. Add the applicable insurance premium if not waived; never add the fees subtotal twice.
